items.title: Agentick: A Unified Benchmark for General Sequential Decision-Making Agents
items.abstract: Agentick is a unified benchmark designed to fairly evaluate diverse sequential decision-making agents, including RL, LLM, and hybrid approaches. It offers 37 procedurally generated tasks across various capabilities, difficulties, and modalities through a single interface. Agentick's contribution lies in enabling direct comparison of agent types and facilitating research into fundamental sequential decision-making challenges.
items.figure_caption: Two observation modalities for KeyDoorPuzzle at medium difficulty. Left: isometric pixel rendering (512 × \( \times \) 512 by default, resizable for RL preprocessing) for VLM agents, CNN-based RL, and human play. Right: ASCII grid for LLM agents; the agent ( ˆ ) must collect the gold key ( Kg ), open the gold door ( Dg ), then the red key ( Kr ) and red door ( Dr ) to reach the goal ( G ). The same state also produces natural language, structured dictionary, and numpy array observations.

items.title: Calibrated Enough to Know, Not Calibrated to Act: Fabricated Evidence Makes LLM Agents Commit to the Unknowable
items.abstract: This paper demonstrates that Large Language Model (LLM) agents are highly susceptible to fabricated evidence, committing to actions on unknowable questions when presented with professional-looking data. The core method involves comparing LLM agent responses to provably unpredictable questions with and without fabricated market panels, showing a significant increase in confident action. The contribution highlights that the authority of the evidence's packaging, rather than its factual content, drives LLM decision-making, even when the underlying information is false.

items.title: CODESKILL: Learning Self-Evolving Skills for Coding Agents
items.abstract: CODESKILL is a novel LLM-based framework that learns to manage a bank of reusable coding skills. It extracts, evolves, and maintains these skills from agent trajectories using a learned policy, addressing limitations of fixed prompts and heuristic updates. This self-evolving skill bank allows coding agents to more effectively learn and adapt to new tasks.

items.title: Combee: Scaling Prompt Learning for Self-Improving Language Model Agents
items.abstract: Combee is a novel framework designed to scale prompt learning for self-improving language model agents. Its core method addresses the limitations of existing approaches by enabling efficient and high-quality parallel prompt learning, allowing agents to learn from a large number of traces without performance degradation. This contribution significantly improves the efficiency and effectiveness of agents that learn and adapt over time.

items.title: DIAL: Position-Debiased LLM Judges with Adaptive Human Preference Calibration
items.abstract: DIAL is a framework that uses both abundant LLM comparisons and limited human feedback to improve LLM-based evaluations. It debiases LLM judgments by accounting for response order and then calibrates these debiased LLM preferences to better align with actual human preferences. This approach allows for more scalable and accurate LLM evaluations by leveraging LLMs while ensuring they reflect human values.
items.figure_caption: Overview of DIAL framework. (a) Pairwise evaluation combines abundant, scalable LLM judgments with limited, higher-fidelity human judgments. (b) Empirical examples illustrate two distinct challenges: position bias and human-preference misalignment. (c) DIAL jointly models LLM and human comparisons to separate judge-specific position effects from latent LLM preferences, learn shared preference structure across judges, and adaptively calibrate toward human preference.

items.title: Estimating and Orthogonalizing Unknown Pre-training Gradients for Continual Fine-tuning of Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper proposes EoupCT, a novel framework to address catastrophic forgetting in continual LLM fine-tuning. EoupCT estimates unknown pre-training gradients by generating pseudo-data via a learnable soft prompt, allowing for orthogonalization and preservation of general-purpose knowledge lost during fine-tuning. This approach aims to overcome limitations of existing methods that require inaccessible pre-training data.

items.title: FTB Graph: Determining and Validating First-token Broadcasters and Language-Identity Head Circuits in Multilingual Language Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces FTB Graph, a method using Edge Attribution Patching and activation patching to map the causal circuits responsible for determining the target language of multilingual language models. The core contribution is the discovery of "broadcasting hubs" in deep or mid-to-deep layers that dictate first-token language identity, with variations observed across different model architectures.
items.figure_caption: Overview of the proposed first-token broadcasting circuit-discovery pipeline. The workflow begins with dataset preparation, model instrumentation, and token-level auditing; applies node attribution and Edge Attribution Patching (EAP) to identify candidate circuit edges; verifies the shortlisted edges using exact activation patching; constructs the resulting directed acyclic graph; and validates the discovered circuit through topological analysis and causal ablation experiments.

items.title: G$^2$PTQ: Improving LLM Post-Training Quantization with Generalized Gradient Compensation
items.abstract: G$^2$PTQ improves LLM post-training quantization by unifying first- and second-order gradient information within a globally supervised, block-wise optimization. It addresses limitations of prior methods by dynamically refreshing gradient and Hessian estimates for each Transformer block and stabilizing updates with a trust-region scaling mechanism. This approach leads to more accurate and efficient LLM quantization.

items.title: HasMem: Hard-Origin Adaptively Softened Memory for Long-Term LLM Agents
items.abstract: HasMem introduces a novel memory system for long-term LLM agents that combines a fixed, verifiable "hard-origin" prompt with an adaptively softened memory. This approach allows for flexible memory resizing and re-encoding without altering the frozen LLM, significantly improving long-term context retention and question answering performance on complex multi-session tasks.

items.title: MoMHa: Multi-Objective Optimization of LLM Harnesses over Accuracy, Safety, and Tokens
items.abstract: This paper introduces MoMHa, a novel method for optimizing the Python code (harness) that surrounds Large Language Models. MoMHa treats harness design as a multi-objective search problem, balancing accuracy, safety, and token cost. Its core contribution is demonstrating that a single-phase joint-reward approach for this search outperforms other strategies, leading to better overall harness performance.

items.title: PUBG Ally: A Conversational Embodied Agent as an AI Teammate
items.abstract: PUBG Ally is a conversational embodied agent designed to act as an AI teammate in the game PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS. Its core method combines a language model for reasoning and communication with a fast control layer for real-time game actions, enabling it to perceive the game, interact naturally with players, and make strategic decisions. The paper's contribution lies in demonstrating this integrated approach to creating a responsive and engaging AI teammate, trained on extensive real-world gameplay data.
items.figure_caption: PUBG Ally as a Co-Playable Character (CPC). Ally shares a live match with a human player, communicating through voice while taking in-game actions as an AI teammate. The figure highlights representative interactions throughout a match: suggesting a drop location, supporting the player during looting, calling out enemies while rotating, and deploying smoke to revive a downed player. Together, these examples illustrate how Ally observes the evolving game state, coordinates with the player, and acts autonomously as a co-playable character in the shared game world.

items.title: Rufus-Air: An Open LLM Post-Training Recipe
items.abstract: Rufus-Air presents an open, eight-stage post-training recipe for LLMs, building capabilities sequentially from supervised fine-tuning to advanced agentic reasoning. Its core contribution is a reproducible methodology using open-source components and public data, emphasizing reward reliability and difficulty filtering for effective training without new human annotation.
items.figure_caption: Recipe overview. The post-training pipeline runs from the GLM-4.5-Air-Base checkpoint through eight stages to the final Rufus-Air model, each stage trained on the checkpoint the previous one produced.

items.title: Stepwise Intrinsic Rewards for Reasoning in Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces Stepwise Marginal Information Gain (MIG), an intrinsic reward signal for training LLMs in reinforcement learning. MIG measures how each reasoning step improves the likelihood of the correct answer, rewarding progress without requiring external annotations or complex search. This allows for more granular feedback during training, guiding LLMs towards better reasoning by identifying beneficial intermediate steps.

items.title: StraTA: Incentivizing Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Strategic Trajectory Abstraction
items.abstract: This paper introduces StraTA, a framework that enhances agentic reinforcement learning for long-horizon tasks by incorporating an explicit, sampled trajectory-level strategy. This strategy guides the agent's actions, improving exploration and credit assignment. StraTA's core contribution is this strategic abstraction, which jointly trains strategy generation and action execution, leading to significant improvements in sample efficiency and final performance across various challenging benchmarks.
items.figure_caption: A comparison between reactive agent and our proposed StraTA framework. (a) Reactive agent generates actions from local states alone, planning and executing at the same time, which may lead to short-sighted exploration, unnecessary backtracking, and inconsistent behavior. (b) StraTA framework first generates a compact global strategy and conditions all subsequent actions on this, enabling more coherent and consistent execution. (c) On long-horizon agentic tasks, explicit strategy guidance significantly improves learning efficiency and final performance.

items.title: The Geometry of Refusal: Why Post-Hoc Safety Is Fragile and Pretraining-Time Safety Persists
items.abstract: This paper argues that post-hoc safety training methods like RLHF are fragile because they create a "refusal gate" that masks, rather than erases, undesirable behaviors. Geometrically, these safety updates are orthogonal to the model's core capabilities, meaning they only suppress them slightly on sharp curvature directions. Consequently, even minor benign fine-tuning can easily restore the original, unsafe capabilities.

items.title: Think Short, Defer Smart, Act, and Repeat: Calibrated Reasoning and Uncertainty-Aware Deferral for Edge LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces Think Short, Defer Smart (TSDS), a framework for edge LLM agents. TSDS efficiently manages on-device reasoning by stopping early when an action is stable and intelligently defers uncertain actions to a cloud model using perplexity. Its core contribution is a jointly calibrated approach that optimizes both task performance and resource usage on edge devices.

items.title: VLANeXt Family: A Systematic Study of VLA Models from Core Recipes to Emerging Paradigms
items.abstract: This paper systematically studies Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models by dissecting design choices across foundational components, perception, and action modeling. Their core method involves a unified framework and evaluation setup, starting from a baseline similar to RT-2. The key contribution is distilling 12 findings into a practical recipe for building strong VLA models, exemplified by their proposed VLANeXt.

items.title: Why Jailbreaks Succeed in Diffusion Language Models: An Energy Landscape Analysis
items.abstract: This paper explains jailbreaks in diffusion language models by viewing safety alignment as an energy landscape. Jailbreaks succeed by either hiding the harmful intent initially or forcing the generation process over an "energy barrier" towards unsafe outputs. The authors propose three training-free detection methods based on analyzing the initial query and the generation's trajectory, offering a unified framework for understanding and detecting these attacks.

items.title: Admission Without Answers: Label-Free Certification and Experience Learning for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling
items.abstract: This paper introduces ADMITOR, a novel label-free method for admitting reliable optimization models generated by LLMs. ADMITOR achieves this by generating multiple models, testing them on resampled problem instances, and admitting those with consistent optimal values across different model families. Its key contribution is enabling robust experience learning for LLM-based optimization without requiring ground-truth answers, significantly improving the precision of admitted candidate models.

items.title: Affective Flow Language Model for Emotional Support Conversation
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Affective Flow Language Model (AFlow) to improve emotional support conversations. AFlow models the dialogue as an "affective utility flow," allowing it to estimate the value of intermediate conversation states and potential strategies. Its contribution lies in the Affective Flow Preference Optimization (AFPO) method, which uses this flow concept to propagate feedback from overall dialogue success to guide the model's sequential strategy decisions in multi-turn interactions.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of emotional support conversation approaches.

papers.title: MoMHa: Multi-Objective Optimization of LLM Harnesses over Accuracy, Safety, and Tokens
papers.abstract: This paper introduces MoMHa, a novel method for optimizing the Python code (harness) that surrounds Large Language Models. MoMHa treats harness design as a multi-objective search problem, balancing accuracy, safety, and token cost. Its core contribution is demonstrating that a single-phase joint-reward approach for this search outperforms other strategies, leading to better overall harness performance.

papers.title: PUBG Ally: A Conversational Embodied Agent as an AI Teammate
papers.abstract: PUBG Ally is a conversational embodied agent designed to act as an AI teammate in the game PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS. Its core method combines a language model for reasoning and communication with a fast control layer for real-time game actions, enabling it to perceive the game, interact naturally with players, and make strategic decisions. The paper's contribution lies in demonstrating this integrated approach to creating a responsive and engaging AI teammate, trained on extensive real-world gameplay data.
papers.figure_caption: PUBG Ally as a Co-Playable Character (CPC). Ally shares a live match with a human player, communicating through voice while taking in-game actions as an AI teammate. The figure highlights representative interactions throughout a match: suggesting a drop location, supporting the player during looting, calling out enemies while rotating, and deploying smoke to revive a downed player. Together, these examples illustrate how Ally observes the evolving game state, coordinates with the player, and acts autonomously as a co-playable character in the shared game world.

papers.title: Rufus-Air: An Open LLM Post-Training Recipe
papers.abstract: Rufus-Air presents an open, eight-stage post-training recipe for LLMs, building capabilities sequentially from supervised fine-tuning to advanced agentic reasoning. Its core contribution is a reproducible methodology using open-source components and public data, emphasizing reward reliability and difficulty filtering for effective training without new human annotation.
papers.figure_caption: Recipe overview. The post-training pipeline runs from the GLM-4.5-Air-Base checkpoint through eight stages to the final Rufus-Air model, each stage trained on the checkpoint the previous one produced.

papers.title: Stepwise Intrinsic Rewards for Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Stepwise Marginal Information Gain (MIG), an intrinsic reward signal for training LLMs in reinforcement learning. MIG measures how each reasoning step improves the likelihood of the correct answer, rewarding progress without requiring external annotations or complex search. This allows for more granular feedback during training, guiding LLMs towards better reasoning by identifying beneficial intermediate steps.

papers.title: StraTA: Incentivizing Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Strategic Trajectory Abstraction
papers.abstract: This paper introduces StraTA, a framework that enhances agentic reinforcement learning for long-horizon tasks by incorporating an explicit, sampled trajectory-level strategy. This strategy guides the agent's actions, improving exploration and credit assignment. StraTA's core contribution is this strategic abstraction, which jointly trains strategy generation and action execution, leading to significant improvements in sample efficiency and final performance across various challenging benchmarks.
papers.figure_caption: A comparison between reactive agent and our proposed StraTA framework. (a) Reactive agent generates actions from local states alone, planning and executing at the same time, which may lead to short-sighted exploration, unnecessary backtracking, and inconsistent behavior. (b) StraTA framework first generates a compact global strategy and conditions all subsequent actions on this, enabling more coherent and consistent execution. (c) On long-horizon agentic tasks, explicit strategy guidance significantly improves learning efficiency and final performance.

papers.title: The Geometry of Refusal: Why Post-Hoc Safety Is Fragile and Pretraining-Time Safety Persists
papers.abstract: This paper argues that post-hoc safety training methods like RLHF are fragile because they create a "refusal gate" that masks, rather than erases, undesirable behaviors. Geometrically, these safety updates are orthogonal to the model's core capabilities, meaning they only suppress them slightly on sharp curvature directions. Consequently, even minor benign fine-tuning can easily restore the original, unsafe capabilities.

papers.title: Think Short, Defer Smart, Act, and Repeat: Calibrated Reasoning and Uncertainty-Aware Deferral for Edge LLM Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Think Short, Defer Smart (TSDS), a framework for edge LLM agents. TSDS efficiently manages on-device reasoning by stopping early when an action is stable and intelligently defers uncertain actions to a cloud model using perplexity. Its core contribution is a jointly calibrated approach that optimizes both task performance and resource usage on edge devices.

papers.title: VLANeXt Family: A Systematic Study of VLA Models from Core Recipes to Emerging Paradigms
papers.abstract: This paper systematically studies Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models by dissecting design choices across foundational components, perception, and action modeling. Their core method involves a unified framework and evaluation setup, starting from a baseline similar to RT-2. The key contribution is distilling 12 findings into a practical recipe for building strong VLA models, exemplified by their proposed VLANeXt.

papers.title: Why Jailbreaks Succeed in Diffusion Language Models: An Energy Landscape Analysis
papers.abstract: This paper explains jailbreaks in diffusion language models by viewing safety alignment as an energy landscape. Jailbreaks succeed by either hiding the harmful intent initially or forcing the generation process over an "energy barrier" towards unsafe outputs. The authors propose three training-free detection methods based on analyzing the initial query and the generation's trajectory, offering a unified framework for understanding and detecting these attacks.

papers.title: Admission Without Answers: Label-Free Certification and Experience Learning for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling
papers.abstract: This paper introduces ADMITOR, a novel label-free method for admitting reliable optimization models generated by LLMs. ADMITOR achieves this by generating multiple models, testing them on resampled problem instances, and admitting those with consistent optimal values across different model families. Its key contribution is enabling robust experience learning for LLM-based optimization without requiring ground-truth answers, significantly improving the precision of admitted candidate models.

papers.title: Affective Flow Language Model for Emotional Support Conversation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the Affective Flow Language Model (AFlow) to improve emotional support conversations. AFlow models the dialogue as an "affective utility flow," allowing it to estimate the value of intermediate conversation states and potential strategies. Its contribution lies in the Affective Flow Preference Optimization (AFPO) method, which uses this flow concept to propagate feedback from overall dialogue success to guide the model's sequential strategy decisions in multi-turn interactions.
papers.figure_caption: Comparison of emotional support conversation approaches.
